answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity with mirrored audit trails: before an agent can trade in the orchard marketplace, it must lock a copper-denominated bond and publish a verifiable history of completed work. Peers mirror that record, so a fake identity starts with no reputation and must pay the full bond and build real history to gain trust. Creating thousands of sock puppets then costs thousands of bonds plus genuine work, while honest agents pay once and reuse their record, making mass fakery uneconomical.
